title: Tesla owner Max Paul Franklin reports that FSD v12 drove him 13 miles to a VA emergency room during an insulin-pump failure at 2 a.m. in North Carolina
summary: By his own X account, FSD v12 drove Max Paul Franklin 13 miles to a VA emergency room at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024; uncorroborated.
account: By his own account, posted on X on 10 April 2024, Max Paul Franklin, a North Carolina television producer, had severe dehydration and a blood glucose reading of 670 at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024 after his insulin pump malfunctioned. He says he got into his Tesla Model Y, engaged the Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 trial unlocked the day before, and that the car drove the 13 miles to the VA emergency room (Charles George VA Medical Center, Asheville, per Il Fatto Quotidiano) without intervention and offered to park. He reports a mild heart attack and discharge with no restrictions. Tesla and Elon Musk reposted it on 11 April 2024; no hospital or official source has confirmed it.
purpose: FSD (Supervised) is built to navigate a Tesla to a chosen destination while an attentive driver supervises it; driving Franklin to the destination he set is that function. Use by a driver impaired by a medical emergency is not an intended use: Hindustan Times notes the system depends on driver intervention when needed, and a Tesla owner quoted by Tesla Oracle calls it a Level 2 system that requires hands on the wheel and eyes on the road even when active.
system: Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 on a Tesla Model Y
model_version: FSD v12 (Supervised), unlocked on the car on 1 April 2024 per Franklin and Tesla Oracle; the exact build is not stated (The Driven describes the then-current release as 12.3.3)
domain: Road transport / access to emergency care
segment: Consumer driver-assistance software on a privately owned vehicle
taxonomy_note: No listed type covers emergency transport. Chosen because, on his account, the driving automation gave a driver impaired by a hyperglycaemic episode access to an emergency room at 2 a.m. The Monitor entry's harm field (Economic/Property damage) comes from unrelated reports of FSD curb strikes bundled into the same entry and has no bearing on this drive.

ratings.reason: By his own account Franklin reached a VA emergency room during an insulin-pump failure with a blood glucose reading of 670, was treated for a mild heart attack and left with no restrictions. No clinician, hospital or official source confirms the emergency, the drive or that his life was at risk, so the life-saving claim in the headlines is not established and -3 or -4 is not supported.

ai_role.statement: The only description of what FSD did is Franklin's: engaged by a double click of the stalk, it drove the 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention and offered to park on arrival. No Tesla vehicle data, dashcam footage, hospital record, emergency-service log or official statement has been found, and no outlet reports having interviewed him or the hospital; Tesla's corporate account and Elon Musk reposted the story on 11 April 2024 but added no facts. The photos attached to the post (two hospital-bed selfies and a night shot of a Model Y in a wet car park) show no route, timestamp or hospital name. Some syndicated coverage garbles the story (Sky TG24 places him in Virginia and describes low blood sugar). The counterfactual, calling emergency services, driving himself or not reaching care, is unexamined; commenters cited by Il Fatto Quotidiano argued he should have called for help.

produced_by: A Tesla Model Y with the FSD (Supervised) v12 trial active, which Franklin says Tesla had unlocked for all US cars on 1 April 2024
A driver who, by his account, could still reach the car, engage FSD with a double click of the stalk and set the emergency room as the destination
A 13-mile route to the VA emergency room that the system, on his account, completed without intervention and then offered to park
must_hold: FSD (Supervised) requires an attentive driver with hands on the wheel and eyes on the road (Hindustan Times; Tesla Oracle quoting owner James Locke); a driver too impaired to supervise would be outside its intended use

The account is Franklin's alone: no hospital, emergency-service, police or vehicle-log record of the drive has been found, and the photos attached to the post do not show the route, a timestamp or the hospital
Emergency services remain the documented first resort; Il Fatto Quotidiano reports commenters arguing that he should have called for help
